newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Police recover stolen Swiss grenades, bust ring.
newsitem.headline: Police recover stolen Swiss grenades, bust ring.

text.p: Swiss and German police broke up a weapons ring and recovered more than 400 of 448 practice hand grenades stolen from a Swiss army munitions dump in April, authorities said on Friday.

Police in the German state of Bavaria tipped off their Swiss counterparts that an Austrian drugs and weapons merchant living in Zurich had added grenades to his wares on offer, Bavarian investigator Wolfgang Sommer told a news conference.

Undercover officers finally set up a deal with the 32-year-old suspect, who was detained on Thursday. Four Swiss who allegedly broke into the munitions dump were also in custody, as was one suspect's girlfriend, officials said.
Police seized 405 of the missing grenades, which, although meant for training, are still deadly within a radius of five metres (yards). They also secured explosives, fuses, weapons and ammunition.
The search was still on for the other missing grenades.
